article.articleHeadline: Three Doctors Talk Health: As temperatures drop sharply, how can primary and secondary school students prevent the flu?
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-23, influenza is in a high-incidence phase in Qingdao as temperatures fluctuate. Primary and secondary school students are a key at-risk group due to crowding and developing immunity. Winter classrooms promote spread because of cold, dry air, reduced ventilation, and close contact. Preventive measures for students include strict hand hygiene, covering coughs and sneezes, regular ventilation of homes and classrooms, and wearing masks in crowded or enclosed settings. Vaccination against influenza is the most effective preventive tool and should be offered to eligible students. Also, maintain regular routines, avoid sharing personal items, and stay home when feverish; seek medical care early for persistent fever, malaise, or muscle pain.

article.articleHeadline: Looks cute, is it harmless? Once it develops, the fatality rate is 100%!
article.articleSummary: Rabies outbreak in Wuhan, China: two confirmed cases admitted to Wuhan Jinyintan Hospital's ICU in November 2026. Patient A was scratched by a two-month-old unvaccinated puppy two months prior; Patient B was licked by a less-than-one-month-old puppy in July. Both developed classic rabies symptoms (hydrophobia, fear of wind and water, throat tightness, difficulty swallowing) and died after symptom onset. Rabies virus is present in saliva and can infect via bites, scratches, or saliva contacting broken skin or mucosa; the extent of bleeding is not related to infection risk. Puppies can carry rabies through maternal transmission or exposure to infected animals. Post-exposure management follows the ‘rinse, disinfect, vaccinate’ protocol: wash wounds with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes, apply antiseptic, then seek prompt vaccination and, if indicated, rabies immunoglobulin. The claim that vaccination after 24 hours is ineffective is debunked; vaccination remains protective if started after exposure. Public health message: even cute puppies can pose serious risk; seek timely medical care after exposure.

article.articleSummary: At a single center in Fujian, China, 33 children (median age 3 years; range 2 months–16 years) with scrub typhus were analyzed; 12 met HLH-2004 criteria for hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis. article.articleHeadline: Western Diet Drives Salmonella to the Liver in Mice.
article.articleSummary: Western-style high-fat, low-fiber diet in mice accelerates Salmonella Enteritidis infection severity and hepatic dissemination. After three weeks on a Western diet (~60% of calories from fat) vs a grain-based control (~17%), mice showed altered gut microbiota with reduced diversity before illness. When challenged with Salmonella Enteritidis at low or high dose, Western-diet mice developed more severe disease and died sooner: at low dose, average time to death was about 15 days versus ~22 days on control diet; high-dose also led to earlier mortality. Despite shedding less bacteria in feces on days 2, 4, and 6, Western-diet mice harbored more Salmonella in liver and spleen, indicating greater systemic spread. Analyses combined 16S rRNA sequencing with metagenomics of both intestinal and hepatic microbiota. The study, conducted in China (Fudan University) and Georgia State University, used 8 mice per group (all male) and was published in Animal Microbiome.

article.articleSummary: COVID-19 SARS-CoV-2 spread in Hong Kong across five waves (2020–2022) was shaped by dense urban cores and subway mobility. Wave 3 and 4 were driven by B.1.1.63 and B.1.36.27; wave 5 by Omicron BA.2.2, infecting roughly 45% of residents and causing substantial elderly mortality. article.articleHeadline: Choking Off Viral Invasion at the Mingmen Gate
article.articleSummary: HBV (hepatitis B virus) entry into hepatocytes is mediated by the NTCP receptor, a gateway identified after 18 years of work by Li Wenhui and Su Jianhua’s team in Beijing. Using tree shrews as the infection model, they mapped hepatocyte gene expression to isolate NTCP as the viral entry portal for the PreS1 domain. Through extensive antibody engineering and screening, lead human monoclonal antibody 2H5-A14 showed strong neutralization and could recruit macrophages and natural killer cells to clear infected cells. The antibody drug Libevita (立贝韦塔) advanced from target discovery to clinical translation, and in October 2024 secured conditional approval in China for hepatitis D virus (HDV) therapy, based on a multinational trial enrolling over 100 patients in China, Pakistan, and Mongolia. The program also established a reusable platform for NTCP research, infection models, and antibody engineering, with next-gen formats including subcutaneous antibodies, oral NTCP inhibitors, and a new core molecule SCARF2.

article.articleHeadline: Don't underestimate a fishbone puncture wound; Vibrio vulnificus infection can be fatal.
article.articleSummary: Vibrio vulnificus infection from a fishbone puncture in Shenzhen, China, led to rapid, life-threatening illness. A 69-year-old man’s small hand wound after handling tilapia progressed within 12–72 hours to high fever, spreading redness, swelling, and painful blisters; he required intensive care at Shenzhen Third People’s Hospital. Laboratory testing confirmed Vibrio vulnificus, a halophilic marine bacterium living in warm seawater and salted water, commonly found in shellfish and shrimp. Transmission occurs via wound contamination from seawater or contaminated seafood, or by consuming raw or undercooked seafood (notably raw oysters). Wound infection can worsen quickly with necrosis; foodborne illness causes fever, chills, nausea, vomiting, and diarrhea, and may lead to necrotizing fasciitis or septicemia with high mortality. Prevention includes avoiding seafood handling with open wounds, wearing waterproof gloves, sanitizing tools, cooking seafood thoroughly, and seeking urgent care if symptoms worsen.

article.articleHeadline: Ruto, Tshisekedi call for regional cooperation to tackle Ebola epidemic
article.articleSummary: Kenya President William Ruto and Democratic Republic of Congo President Félix Tshisekedi urged stronger regional cooperation to eradicate the Ebola epidemic, issuing a joint communiqué after the Quadripartite Political Summit in Oyo, Republic of the Congo, on November 22, 2026. The leaders—joined by Denis Sassou N'Guesso of the Republic of the Congo and Faure Gnassingbé of Togo (AU mediator for eastern DRC security concerns)—emphasised that public health must be addressed through collective action. The communiqué recognises the particularly serious consequences of Ebola and calls for multi-country collaboration, though it does not outline specific measures, funding, or timelines. The summit also underscored broader regional cooperation through the ICGLR and the East African Community (EAC) and committed to diplomacy, dialogue, and African solidarity to prevent disputes from undermining stability. Public health cooperation was framed within strengthening bilateral ties and regional resilience.

article.articleHeadline: Over 10,000 infected: Norway sends 18.3 million.

Funds will support health care for children and mothers, vaccination programs, and relief for health workers, as well as improved sanitation in primary schools, information campaigns, and preventive infection control to protect children and minimize disruption to schooling and transmission. Development Minister Åsmund Aukrust described the outbreak as serious and emphasized global health security and international cooperation; he spoke at an African health summit in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. Norway has also pledged 1 billion NOK to CEPI to support vaccine development, including this Ebola variant.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Beni: a school implements alternating teaching to limit the risk of transmission - ACP
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak in Beni, North Kivu, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, prompts the Wasomi private school to adopt an alternating attendance system to limit transmission. Classes are restructured to halve or third the number of students per session, with preschool, primary (grades 1, 3, 5, 6), and secondary all participating in staggered schedules. Under the plan, students who studied today stay home tomorrow for independent work, with rotations continuing until the end of the first term. Each child must have a personal hand sanitizer; parents are urged to reinforce barrier measures and physical distancing at home and avoid crowded or high-risk places such as funerals, birthday or wedding ceremonies, and hospitals. Four weeks remain in the first term of 2026-2027—two weeks of classes and two weeks of periodic exams. The provincial Director of National Education rejected temporary suspension, arguing schools better protect pupils than home isolation.

article.articleHeadline: DRC: Students educated about their rights and Ebola prevention in Lubero.

Joselyne Nzenze Mutsumbirwa, CFIS coordinator, said the initiative also aims to empower children as sensitization messengers within their families and communities, including those from conflict-affected areas and some internally displaced. The 2026 World Children's Day theme was 'Mon monde, mes droits, mon avenir'.

article.articleHeadline: Why the Ebola Outbreak Keeps Growing, According to Virus Expert Pardis Sabeti
article.articleSummary: Ebola outbreak centered in the Democratic Republic of Congo is the second-largest on record, with over 11,000 cases across five countries and more than 5,700 deaths as of Nov. 20. Pardis Sabeti of the Broad Institute notes that conflict-zone conditions—population movement, refugees, poor sanitation, and breakdowns in healthcare—plus reduced surveillance and global funding cuts hinder containment. The outbreak involves multiple Ebola variants, including Bundibugyo, for which no universal diagnostic exists to detect all circulating strains. Stigmatization and secrecy about illness impede public health responses. Operation Outbreak, an education tool simulating outbreak spread, diagnosis, vaccination decisions, and epidemiology, is being used in 27 U.S. states and 20 countries and piloted with the UN, World Health Organization, and the FBI to improve preparedness.

article.articleHeadline: Ebola in Bafwasende: a joint mission assesses the conditions for resuming the outbreak response.

Led by Michel Bakay (provincial Interior Minister) with the Health Minister and humanitarian partners (OCHA, UNICEF, IOM, WHO) alongside the provincial health division, the team aims to restore trust with communities and restart outbreak activities, including surveillance and treatment. Emphasis was on proper use of insecticide-treated nets, environmental management, and promptly seeking care for fever, while avoiding self-medication. CJP-Asbl, also called the Army of Youth against Malaria, began in June 2022 and officially launched in Kinshasa on 27 November 2023, aiming to mobilize youth (15–35) against malaria, NTDs, HIV/AIDS, and TB, and to promote universal health coverage across 16 provincial coordinations.

article.articleHeadline: UK Study Identifies 38 Percent Error Rate in Malaria Prescriptions
article.articleSummary: Two UK secondary-care hospitals (Queen Elizabeth Hospital Birmingham; Birmingham Heartlands Hospital) conducted a retrospective quality‑improvement study of adult imported malaria diagnosed Jan 2023–Dec 2025, including 91 patients with laboratory-confirmed malaria. Nigeria accounted for 35% of travel-associated cases, followed by Congo, Sudan, Sierra Leone; Pakistan 15%, India, Bangladesh, with 38% reporting mosquito bites. Malaria was the initial working diagnosis in 64% of presentations. Rapid diagnostic testing was positive in all cases; peripheral blood films failed to visualise parasites in three. Plasmodium falciparum predominated (66%), P. vivax 27%; 12% had parasitaemia >2%; two required ICU. Time from laboratory diagnosis to the first antimalarial dose was seven hours, driven by drug stock issues and prescribing inaccuracies. Length of stay 3 days. Authors propose standardised malaria pathways, mandatory infectious diseases consultation, electronic prescribing with dose validation, improved pharmacy stock governance, and multidisciplinary audits to reduce delays and errors in imported malaria care.

article.articleHeadline: 'Dr. Yong' concerned about a severe diphtheria outbreak; recommends vaccination and booster shots every 10 years.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 November 2026, Thailand faces a diphtheria outbreak along the southern border. Diphtheria causes throat infection with white patches, potential airway obstruction requiring tracheostomy, and cervical lymphadenopathy (bull neck); myocarditis and neuropathy are feared complications, with historical mortality around 50%. The diphtheria toxoid vaccine prevents toxin-mediated disease but not infection; high vaccine coverage is essential for herd immunity. Optimal herd immunity is cited at ≥85%, with coverage ideally above 90%. Immunity wanes over time, hence boosters every 10 years. Two waning-immunity groups are identified: those never vaccinated and those vaccinated but not boosted; many older adults may have natural immunity from past exposure. Studies suggest individuals vaccinated in childhood should receive boosters in adulthood, particularly ages 20–50, to curb ongoing transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Pediatric Chikungunya Encephalitis Cases Documented in Northern Thailand
article.articleSummary: Two pediatric cases of chikungunya-associated encephalitis were documented in northern Thailand’s Chiang Mai Province during seasonal outbreaks. Case 1 involved a term neonate with vertical transmission from a mother who exhibited fever, rash, and arthralgia near delivery. On day 5 of life the infant developed high fever and edema; CSF showed pleocytosis (44 cells/mm³: 39% neutrophils, 61% lymphocytes) and elevated protein (147 mg/dL) with normal glucose; chikungunya RNA was detected by RT-PCR in serum and CSF, while dengue, Zika, and bacterial tests were negative. The neonate had neonatal jaundice requiring phototherapy and a 28-day hospitalization for pneumonia, followed by normal neurological development at 6 and 12 months. Case 2 was an 11-year-old from Hang Dong District, a community-acquired infection presenting with fever, rapid encephalopathy, conjunctival injection, and a morbilliform rash without arthritis; labs showed leukocytosis (13,100/µL) and systemic inflammation. Both recovered fully with supportive care. In 2025, Chiang Mai province reported 484 chikungunya cases (30/100k), with Hang Dong District accounting for 319 cases across two outbreaks and a local incidence of 346/100k.

article.articleHeadline: Cambodia Confirms First Mpox Case in 30 Months
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) has been confirmed in Cambodia—the first case in about 30 months—after a patient tested positive on 20 November 2026 and hospitalized, with official confirmation on 22 November 2026. No details on the patient’s age, sex, nationality or location were released, and the infection source and close contacts have not been disclosed. Cambodia previously recorded 20 mpox cases from December 2023 to May 2024. The health ministry urged vigilance to prevent clusters; no vaccination measures were announced for this case. Key symptoms include a blistering rash (face, limbs, body, eyes, mouth or genitals) with fever, swollen lymph nodes, headache, muscle aches and fatigue. Mpox spreads mainly through close or sexual contact, not brief casual contact; most people recover in weeks, though young children, pregnant women and immunocompromised individuals are at higher risk. article.articleHeadline: Used to be only during the rainy season, now dengue fever looms year-round due to climate change.
article.articleSummary: Year-round dengue risk in Indonesia as climate change expands Aedes aegypti breeding; Jakarta and nationwide. In 2025 Indonesia recorded >161,000 dengue cases; by October 2026, 98,946 cases and 265 deaths across 467 regencies/cities. Indonesia ranks second globally in dengue burden after Brazil and is the highest in Southeast Asia. Warmer temperatures accelerate mosquito life cycle and virus replication; La Niña raises rainfall creating more larval habitats; hot spells drive people to store water in open containers, sustaining transmission. Preventive measures emphasized: strict 3M plus—drain and scrub water-holding containers weekly, cover water storage, and reuse discarded containers to avoid standing water; home protection with insect repellent, screens, and mosquito-repellent plants. Support for innovations (Wolbachia-infected mosquitoes) and early-warning weather monitoring by BMKG; vaccination programs for dengue exist but are limited to certain children in some areas. Authorities call for intensified vector-control innovations beyond community action.

article.articleHeadline: Hospital Staff in Brazil Harbor Multidrug-Resistant Staph in Nasal Cavities
article.articleSummary: In a public hospital in Caxias, eastern Maranhão, Brazil, a cross-sectional study (Dec 2024–Feb 2025) found nasal carriage of Staphylococcus aureus in 27.27% of 132 healthcare professionals. Of 36 recovered isolates, 18 (50%) were multidrug-resistant, and 6 (16.67% of colonized; 4.54% of the workforce) met phenotypic criteria for MRSA. The cohort was 68.94% female, mean age 38.94 years (SD 10.90); nursing technicians/assistants comprised 40.91%, registered nurses 26.52% (35 individuals), physicians 21.97% (29), and allied health workers 10.61%. Exclusion: no systemic antibiotics in the two weeks prior to sampling. Isolation involved BHI broth, blood and mannitol salt agars, and MALDI-TOF confirmation (Biotyper 3.1). Disk diffusion against 15 antibiotics showed high resistance to penicillin G and ampicillin (94.44%), erythromycin (83.33%), and azithromycin (77.78%); cefoxitin resistance was 16.67%, with ciprofloxacin 11.11% and levofloxacin 8.33% resistance. Indicates ongoing occupational circulation of high-risk S. aureus lineages in Brazilian hospitals.

article.articleHeadline: Midges pose a growing health threat to Britons, experts warn
article.articleSummary: Midges pose a growing health threat for Britain as potential vectors of animal and human pathogens. The UK, with more than 650 midge species concentrated in Scotland, already harbours midges that spread Bluetongue and Schmallenberg, causing severe illness in livestock. Human risk is highlighted by Shamonda virus: a first-ever human case in France, a death in a patient with terminal cancer, and subsequent detection in animals across Europe; this year UK cattle tested positive for Shamonda for the first time on farms in Shropshire and Powys, Wales. In the Americas, Oropouche virus—also midge-borne—has led to thousands of cases in South and Central America, with Brazil reporting more than 13,000 since 2023 and concerns for pregnancy outcomes. Britain has imported Oropouche cases but no local spread yet; climate warming raises the specter of establishment. UK research: a £3 million PAMEC project at the University of Glasgow will test if Scottish midges can be infected by Oropouche.

The Public Prosecutor’s Office (MP-RO) is investigating and has requested a new arrest warrant amid potential additional victims. Dunga was already convicted in August 2026 to five years in prison under a semi-open regime and ordered to pay 50,000 reais in damages in a case linked to one complainant; another criminal proceeding involves three more women. Prosecutors allege a pattern of pursuing intimate relationships to infect victims, and that Dunga knew his HIV status for about ten years while allegedly not adhering to antiretroviral therapy, potentially enabling transmission. One complainant, anonymized as Marta, describes persistent infections, body pains, redness, itching, headaches, and fatigue before an HIV diagnosis.

article.articleHeadline: Study analyzes dengue, Zika, and Chikungunya in five municipalities of Bico do Papagaio.
article.articleSummary: Dengue, Zika, and Chikungunya are analyzed in five municipalities in the Bico do Papagaio region, northern Tocantins, Brazil (Tocantinópolis, Araguatins, Augustinópolis, São Miguel do Tocantins, Nazaré). Conducted by Unitins at Campus Augustinópolis, the subproject aims to analyze temporal trends and the epidemiological profile of arboviruses from 2016–2025, linking cases to climate factors to support surveillance and vector control. Using Sinan/Datasus, IBGE, and Inmet data, researchers will compute standardized incidence rates and apply Poisson or negative binomial regression for trends, STL for seasonality, and climate correlations with 0–3 month lags, presenting results as choropleth maps in QGIS and inter-municipal comparisons. The project, spanning 24 months, will deliver a Technical Surveillance Manual for Bico do Papagaio, clinician and public health workshops, and publish articles. It aligns with UN SDGs 3, 11, and 13.

article.articleHeadline: What is brucellosis? The disease is now notifiable in Brazil.
article.articleSummary: Brucellosis, a bacterial zoonosis transmitted from animals to humans, is now a nationally notifiable disease in Brazil. A portaria published in the Diário Oficial da União on 17 November 2026 requires health services to report cases weekly to surveillance authorities to improve tracking of a disease that is often underreported. Brucellosis is caused by Brucella spp. and is linked to contact with infected animals and consumption of animal products, especially unpasteurized milk and dairy items, as well as raw or undercooked meat; occupational exposure is common among rural workers, veterinarians, slaughterhouse, and dairy workers. Symptoms include fever, profuse night sweats, chills, weakness, weight loss, headaches, and musculoskeletal pain; incubation is typically 5–60 days. Diagnosis relies on culture, serology, or PCR. Treatment uses antibiotics via SUS; prevention emphasizes pasteurized dairy, fully cooked meat, PPE, and biosafety practices.

article.articleHeadline: Research identifies a new bacterium linked to the disease that attacks corn.
article.articleSummary: Candidatus Phytoplasma zeae is a new bacterium linked to maize red-stem disease, identified in Santa Catarina, Brazil, with samples from the United States (Oklahoma and Iowa). Reclassified from Candidatus Phytoplasma asteris after genome sequencing, the organism is not yet cultured in the lab, hence the 'Candidatus' designation; Zea mays is the only confirmed natural host. A Santa Catarina lineage, MBSP-BR, was selected as the global reference genome to standardize description and detection by laboratories worldwide. The disease spreads via two leafhopper species: Dalbulus maidis (present in Brazil) and Dalbulus elimatus (not recorded in Brazil). In a parallel study, researchers analyzed the microbiome of 171 leafhopper species across 13 countries, assembling 272 novel bacterial genomes from 264 datasets, revealing three major bacterial groups and co-occurrences with phytoplasma and spiroplasma, with implications for biocontrol and enhanced surveillance.

article.articleHeadline: Fiocruz promotes the 18th International Symposium on Schistosomiasis | Fiocruz Portal
article.articleSummary: Rio de Janeiro hosts the 18th International Symposium on Schistosomiasis (Nov 22–25, 2026), organized by Fiocruz under the theme Global Health and Schistosomiasis. The biannual event gathers 80 speakers, half international, to foster South-South cooperation, SUS training, and policy dialogue on control, diagnosis, treatment, vaccination, and public health. The focus centers on Schistosoma mansoni, the parasite behind schistosomiasis (xistose, barriga d’água). The disease occurs in 54 countries across Africa, the Eastern Mediterranean, the Caribbean, Venezuela, and Brazil; in Brazil about 1.5 million people are at risk, especially in the Southeast and Northeast. From 2010–2023 (SINAN) data show: parda 48.27%, white 29.74%, black 8.86%, yellow 0.97%, indigenous 0.28%, unknown 11.88%; men 58.6%, women 41.68%; urban 78.35%, rural 15.97%. WHO aims to eliminate schistosomiasis as a public health problem by 2030, aligning with the SDGs. The program emphasizes sanitation, clean water, vector control, education, primary care, and epidemiology mapping via biological collections.

article.articleHeadline: Picos: Leprosy cases have already surpassed the 2025 total; see symptoms and how to treat.
article.articleSummary: As of 23 November 2026, Picos, Brazil, has diagnosed 21 leprosy (hansen’s disease) cases in 2026, three more than all of 2025 (18). Brazil recorded over 301,000 cases between 2015 and 2024, according to the Ministry of Health Epidemiological Bulletin. Leprosy is a bacterial infection primarily affecting skin and peripheral nerves; typical signs are skin lesions with altered sensation, though nerve involvement can occur without visible lesions. Delayed diagnosis can cause nerve damage, leading to weakness and loss of movement in hands and feet; incubation can extend for years. Transmission occurs from prolonged close contact with an untreated person; isolation in health facilities is not required. Treatment is free via SUS, using a three-drug regimen (rifampicin, dapsone, clofazimine) as PQT-U, for six months (paucibacillary) or twelve months (multibacillary). Early treatment stops transmission; contacts should be evaluated. Local officials project 15–25 cases annually, and 21 in 2026 falls within that range.

article.articleHeadline: Competitive Landscape of the Coxsackievirus Infections Treatment Market Examined Among Top Global Companies
article.articleSummary: Coxsackievirus Infections Treatment Market is forecast to reach $4.51 billion by 2030, up from $3.1 billion in 2025 and $3.35 billion in 2026 (CAGR 7.8–8.0%). Growth is driven by rising hand, foot and mouth disease (HFMD) incidence, the absence of specific antivirals, pediatric vulnerability, hospital-based care models, and seasonal infection patterns. Treatments remain primarily supportive—rest, hydration, fever and pain relief—with more serious cases potentially requiring management of complications such as viral meningitis or myocarditis. HFMD, mainly caused by Coxsackievirus A16 and Enterovirus 71, is a key market driver. North America led the market in 2025, while Asia-Pacific is expected to register the fastest growth. The Indonesian HFMD outbreak in early 2024 (about 6,500 cases in Q1) illustrates high prevalence driving demand for symptom-relief and preventive care. Diagnostic advances and expanded pediatric care underpin the outlook.

article.articleHeadline: Red Betel Leaf Neolignan Inhibits Hepatitis C Virus in Cell Culture Models
article.articleSummary: Crocatin A, a neolignan from red betel leaves (Piper crocatum) collected in East Java, inhibits hepatitis C virus (HCV) replication in vitro, showing potent activity against the Japan fulminant hepatitis 1 (JFH-1) strain in cultured human hepatocytes. The study found antiviral effects from both the crude 70% ethanol leaf extract and the purified compound, with active constituents dispersed across multiple polarity fractions. From 228 g of dried leaves, 26.22 g of crude extract (11.5%) was obtained, then fractionated into nine pools; six fractions inhibited the virus by >80%. Fraction F4 yielded 8.2 mg of crocatin A (0.003% of starting material) after preparative HPLC, with structural confirmation by 1H/13C NMR (24 carbons). Indonesia bears ~1.4 million chronic HCV cases, contributing to a global burden of ~50 million infections and ~244,000 deaths in 2022. The findings highlight ongoing search for affordable antiviral candidates amid limited access to costly, IP-restricted direct-acting antivirals.

article.articleHeadline: There were major measles outbreaks in 57 countries in 2025, and the United States lost its measles elimination status.
article.articleSummary: Measles outbreaks surged globally in 2025, with 57 countries experiencing major epidemics, including India, Pakistan, Indonesia, Ukraine, Nigeria, and Ethiopia. The United States lost its measles elimination status after more than 25 years. First-dose measles vaccination coverage fell from 86% in 2019 to 84% in 2025, far below the 95% herd-immunity target. Vaccine hesitancy and online misinformation are linked to lower uptake. WHO estimates vaccines prevent about 3.5–5 million deaths annually from diseases such as measles, tetanus, diphtheria, and influenza. The article emphasizes vaccines’ safety and effectiveness, explains how the MMR vaccine uses attenuated viruses, and outlines the rigorous testing process, including accelerated pathways seen during the COVID-19 pandemic.

article.articleHeadline: Regency Government Strengthens Early Detection to Prevent Disease Outbreaks in Kolut.

TK Dharma Bakti Pertiwi families voted to discontinue MBG, reflecting parental safety concerns. The incident underscores food-safety oversight for school feeding programs in Malang.

triage.triage_reason: 東ジャワ州マランの学校給食プログラム(MBG)でE. coli汚染による食中毒が発生し、入院者も出ているが、供給元は既に停止され局所的に管理されている。国際的拡大リスクは低いが、国家規模の給食プログラムの食品安全管理として継続的な注視が必要。
triage.notes: 本事例はインドネシアの国家学校給食プログラム(MBG)における食品安全問題であり、ヒト-ヒト感染のリスクはない。供給業者は既に20日間の営業停止、台所運営者も一時閉鎖措置を受けており、地域レベルで対応済み。国家的プログラムであるため社会的関心はあるが、国際的な公衆衛生上の脅威とは言えない。

article.articleHeadline: Health Office: Cross-sector collaboration needed for malaria elimination in Mimika Regency - ANTARA News Central Papua
article.articleSummary: As of 23 November 2026, cross-sector collaboration is essential for malaria elimination in Mimika Regency, Central Papua, Indonesia. The Papua Tengah Health Office (Adinkes) pushes for involvement from government, corporations, banks, and civil society to develop the RAD Malaria Mimika. Fransiska Rahmawati notes that malaria control requires environmental improvements, market management, and better access to health services, not just patient testing and treatment. Non-government partners include CSR-funded companies, banks, BUMD, YPMAK, CHD, PT Petrosea, and Baznas. A two-day multi-sector meeting aims to define roles and produce a joint declaration for malaria elimination in 2027. Mimika is the first Central Papua regency to start the RAD Malaria; TB and HIV/AIDS RADs are planned for 2027. Adinkes promotes social contracting, urging districts to allocate at least Rp50 million to involve civil society; Mimika has earmarked ATM funds in 133 villages (Rp15–20 million per village). Plt. Kepala Dinas Kesehatan Marselino Mameyao stresses broad involvement; IRS has been used, but environmental remediation, water access, waste management, and community engagement are also needed; elimination by 2030 remains the target.

article.articleHeadline: Indonesian Plants Consumed by Wild Orangutans Inhibit Giardia Parasites in
article.articleSummary: Indonesian plants consumed by wild Sumatran orangutans inhibit Giardia intestinalis in vitro. Field work in North Sumatra near Bukit Lawang and Gunung Leuser National Park shows orangutans increase intake of specific leaves during higher parasite burdens, indicating self-medication. Sixteen plant species’ leaves were collected at ~323 m, dried, ground, and subjected to three solvent extracts (water, methanol, methanol–THF). In vitro assays against active Giardia trophozoites under anaerobic culture revealed inhibitory activity for all species in at least one solvent; four species had IC50 < 1 mg/mL, and eight had no prior biological testing. Giardia intestinalis is globally distributed, with cysts and trophozoites causing giardiasis and GI symptoms; 212 outbreaks were reported between 2004–2016. Metronidazole resistance reported at 30–48% among travelers; concerns over side effects and rodent carcinogenicity. The study links primate behavior to potential antiparasitic drug leads and identifies new botanical candidates for therapy.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアの野生オランウータンが摂取する植物がジアルジア原虫の活動を実験室内で抑制
triage.triage_reason: 本記事はオランウータンの自己治療行動と植物由来成分のジアルジア抑制効果に関する学術研究であり、実際の感染症アウトブレイクや公衆衛生事象の報告ではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は動物行動学・薬理学研究であり、ヒトまたは動物における実際の感染症発生事例を報告するものではないため、対象国の発生地域としては該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Kolhapur News: Little girl from Borivade dies with rabies-like symptoms; had not taken the rabies vaccine; incident occurred a month ago.
article.articleSummary: Eight-year-old Revati Santosh Chaugale from Borivade, Panhala taluka, Kolhapur district, Maharashtra, died of rabies-like symptoms during treatment. About a month earlier, a stray dog chased her; she fell and injured her knee, but it was unclear whether she was bitten, so rabies prophylaxis was not given. She developed fear of water and crowds before deteriorating and dying at Kolhapur’s CPR hospital around 2:30 am on Saturday. This marks the district’s third rabies-related death since March 2024 (Srishti Sunil Shinde, 21, died after a dog attack near Nagala Park; attack Feb 3, 2024; death Mar 4, 2024). In Borivade, 6–7 people were bitten by roaming dogs last month, and in Pajjarwadi 25–30 residents were attacked. Doctors advised rabies prophylaxis for 34 contacts and urged stray-dog control.

triage.headline_ja: コールハープルのニュース:ボリヴァデの少女が狂犬病様症状で死亡、狂犬病ワクチン未接種だった、事件は1か月前に発生
triage.triage_reason: 狂犬病による散発的な死亡例であり、インドでは狂犬病は地方病的に発生しているため国際的な異常性は低いが、野犬による多数の咬傷事例が続いており継続的な曝露リスクがあるため経過観察とする。
triage.notes: 地域の野犬による咬傷が多発しており（6-7人、25-30人の被害）、公衆衛生当局による野犬管理と曝露後予防の徹底が課題。狂犬病はヒト-ヒト感染せず、国際的拡大リスクは低い。

article.articleHeadline: Global dengue cases rise 34-fold in three decades
article.articleSummary: Global dengue cases have risen 34-fold since 1990, with 74 million infections across 143 countries through 2024. About 10.7 million cases are missing from WHO databases, signaling undercounting in surveillance. Bangladesh faces a major outbreak: by November 22, 2026, 173,473 hospitalizations and 518 deaths; in the prior 24 hours, 1,519 admissions and 2 deaths, with the Dhaka Division accounting for 755 new admissions. The findings were presented at the ASTMH meeting in National Harbor, Maryland, by Dr. Ahyoung Lim of the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. South Asia shows the fastest growth, with rising cases in Africa and the Middle East; increases reflect both real spread and improved detection, not unique drivers. Dengue, transmitted by Aedes aegypti in urban areas, is influenced by climate, urbanisation, and travel, underscoring the need for stronger surveillance. Dataset includes Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.

triage.headline_ja: 世界のデング熱症例、過去30年間で34倍に増加
triage.triage_reason: 世界的にデング熱症例が急増し、バングラデシュでは大規模な入院・死亡が報告されており、公衆衛生への影響と国際的拡大の両基準に該当するためフルRRAでの評価が望ましい。
triage.notes: 記事の主眼はグローバル動向と特にバングラデシュの流行状況だが、バングラデシュは対象国リストに含まれないため除外。Indiaはデータセットおよび南アジアの急増地域として言及されているため含めた。他の言及国（Pakistan, Nepal, Sri Lanka）は対象国リスト外。

article.articleHeadline: 47 vs 0: Dengue death data exposes surveillance gap in Telangana
article.articleSummary: Telangana recorded 10,077 dengue cases in 2024 with zero deaths per NCVBDC, but death certificates listing dengue as cause totalled 47 per the Registrar General's MCCD, revealing a surveillance gap. From 2021–2025, Telangana logged 46,612 cases, including over 8,000 in 2025, with more than 4,000 cases reported between April and August 2025. Nationally, the MCCD reported 2,340 medically certified dengue deaths in 2024, compared with 297 in NCVBDC, a discrepancy of about 688%. Hyderabad doctors report rising cases this year despite weaker rainfall; fatalities continue. Notable Telangana deaths cited: a four-year-old with acute liver failure, a 60-year-old patient, and a college student. Private-clinic testing and underreporting to vector surveillance contribute to gaps; authorities will review MCCD figures, verify deaths via verbal autopsies, and ensure correct district entries, with prognosis ongoing.

triage.headline_ja: 47対0：デング熱死亡者数データがテランガーナ州のサーベイランスの欠陥を露呈
triage.triage_reason: デング熱はインドで毎年発生する風土病であり、本記事は新規アウトブレイクではなく死亡統計の報告体制（サーベイランスギャップ）の問題を指摘する内容。国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは見られないが、過小報告の実態は公衆衛生上の懸念として継続的な注視が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はテランガーナ州における2024年のデング死亡者数データ（NCVBDC公式0件 vs MCCD死亡証明書47件）の乖離を報告しており、全国的にも2,340件（MCCD）対297件（NCVBDC）と大きな差がある。これは新規アウトブレイクではなく既存の風土病に関する報告システムの問題であり、国際的な公衆衛生リスクとしての緊急性は低いが、国内のサーベイランス体制の脆弱性を示す継続観察事項。

article.articleHeadline: Food poisoning among 37 people who ate mint from a hotel in Kattappana; two are in serious condition.
article.articleSummary: Thirty-seven people developed food poisoning after consuming a mint-based item at a hotel in Kattappana town, Idukki district, near the Civil Station, late Sunday around 11:30 p.m. They all reported abdominal pain and vomiting, with 35 admitted to Kattappana Taluk Hospital for observation and treatment. Two of the patients were in serious condition and were subsequently transferred to Idukki Medical College for specialist care. The affected group included Tirur-based students and other travelers visiting the region. Health department officials visited the hotel and conducted an inspection as part of the response. A total of 37 cases were reported, with 35 admitted.

triage.triage_reason: 単一ホテルでの食中毒事案であり、感染症の国際的拡大や公衆衛生上の重大なリスクは認められない局所的な食品衛生事案である。
triage.notes: 食中毒(食品由来疾患)であり感染症イベントではないため、本SOPの対象外に近い。保健当局がホテルを調査済み。

article.articleHeadline: Tribal Pandemic Response Study Reveals Major Regional Differences in
article.articleSummary: COVID-19 non-pharmaceutical interventions adherence surveyed across four tribal communities in India: Baiga (Dindori, Madhya Pradesh); Bhariya (Patalkot Valley, Chhindwara, MP); Saharia (Shivpuri, MP); Bodh (Keylong, Lahaul and Spiti, Himachal Pradesh). Between Sep 2021 and Feb 2022, n=2,617; fever recognition 73% and vaccine awareness 95% were high, but preventive practices varied by region. Hand hygiene (2,232) and mask wearing (2,179) were most common; social distancing (1,313) least. In Lahaul and Spiti, hand hygiene 98.8%, masks 98.4%, social distancing 67.8% (highest). Baiga Dindori: mask 63.0%, social distancing 27.4% (hand hygiene 90.6%). Bhariya Patalkot Valley: handwashing 72.7%, linked to acute water scarcity. Television was the primary information source (61% overall), highest in Shivpuri (87.4%); Dindori and Chhindwara relied more on frontline health workers and print/radio, with limited use of digital platforms (12.9% in Lahaul and Spiti). Centralized directives failed to account for local topography and social structure, driving regional disparities in preventive practices.

triage.headline_ja: 部族のパンデミック対応研究、予防措置における大きな地域差を明らかに
triage.triage_reason: 2021年9月〜2022年2月に実施された過去の疫学研究報告であり、現在進行中の感染症アウトブレイクや公衆衛生上の緊急事態を示す内容ではない。
triage.notes: 本記事は学術研究（調査研究）の結果報告であり、過去のCOVID-19対応における地域的な予防行動の差異を分析したもの。現時点での新規感染症シグナルには該当しない。

article.articleHeadline: Gorakhpur News: Dengue Threat by the End of November, Health Department Alert.
article.articleSummary: Gorakhpur, India: Dengue threat remains through the end of November 2026, with the Health Department issuing an alert. From January–November 2026, 123 dengue-confirmed cases have been reported, compared with 184 in the same period of 2025 — a reduction of 61. The festival season (Diwali and Chhath Puja) heightens transmission risk due to increased travel. Dengue spreads when an infected person is bitten by a mosquito, which can then bite another person. In 2026, September saw 34 cases and October 35; in 2025, September 31 and October 29. Early-year trends show relatively controlled numbers, with January 4; February and March zero; April 3; May 4; June 5; July 9; August 19; September 34; October 35; November 10 (to date). December 2025 had three cases. Ongoing surveillance and preventive measures are urged. Dr. Nandlal Kushwaha, CMO.

triage.headline_ja: ゴラクプル:11月末までデング熱の脅威、保健局が警戒
triage.triage_reason: インド・ゴラクプルにおける季節性デング熱の発生報告であり、2026年の確定症例数（123件）は前年同期（184件）より減少しており、異常性や重篤性の急増は見られない。
triage.notes: デング熱はインドの風土病的存在であり、本記事は季節性の定例的な保健局アラートである。前年比で症例数が減少しており、特段のシグナルとしての緊急性は低い。媒介感染症であるため長期的な監視は必要だが、現時点ではWATCH水準にも満たないと判断。

article.articleHeadline: Puducherry records two dengue deaths in the last few days
article.articleSummary: Two dengue deaths reported in Puducherry over the last few days: a 19-year-old girl and a 23-year-old man. In the first 19 days of November 2026, 46 dengue cases were recorded in the Union Territory, with 43 in Puducherry region and 3 in Karaikal. Year-to-date dengue cases total 1,362 across the UT, and 1,232 of those are in the Puducherry region. Historical counts show Puducherry region recorded 1,625 (2021), 1,673 (2022), 2,790 (2023), 128 (2024), and 902 (2025). October–November 2026 accounted for 721 cases, while September had 151. Pro-tem Speaker A. Anbalagan submitted a memorandum to Chief Minister N. Rangasamy urging enhanced hospital facilities to treat dengue, citing rising cases and inadequate steps. The report emphasizes case totals and official responses, with no infection source details provided.

triage.triage_reason: インドの特定地域でデング熱の死亡例と季節的な症例増加が報告されており、地元政府も対応を検討しているが、国際的拡大や渡航制限のリスクは低く、季節性流行の範囲内とみられるため経過観察とする。

article.articleHeadline: GCC to identify locked houses to assess risk of mosquito breeding
article.articleSummary: Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) identifies locked houses as dengue-breeding sources in Chennai, alongside 24,389 vacant plots and 8,594 new construction sites at high risk. It will check poorly maintained wells in locked houses and, after mapping high-risk sites, begin mosquito-control measures to prevent a dengue surge. Dengue cases in Chennai have declined in November after rising in September and October: 1,293 in September, 1,174 in October, 375 in November. Of 10.83 lakh houses checked for larval density, 7,498 were positive; 41.95 lakh containers checked, 9,408 positive. GCC plans drone-sprayed biolarvicide along Adyar, Cooum and Buckingham Canal from Napier Bridge to Ennore (Buckingham), Napier Bridge to Maduravoyal (Cooum), and Patinapakkam to River View Colony (Adyar). Residents report stagnant water in storm-water drains; about 40% of drains are blocked, prompting calls for engineering solutions to curb breeding and public health risk.

triage.triage_reason: チェンナイにおける季節性デング熱の通常の予防対策に関する記事で、症例数は減少傾向にあり、異常性や国際的拡大リスクは認められない。

article.articleHeadline: Malaria in Delhi heightens tensions; the pace of dengue slows.
article.articleSummary: Post-COVID, malaria, chikungunya, and Japanese encephalitis rose in Delhi-NCR, while dengue's growth slowed but viral evolution alarms researchers. A January 2026 study by ICMR Vector Control Research Centre analyzes five mosquito-borne diseases from 2014–2024, excluding 2020 pandemic-year data to compare pre- and post-pandemic trends. In the National Capital Region during 2023, 4,045 samples were tested; 3,702 (91.5%) harbored dengue virus serotype 2. CSIR-IGIB reported mutations in dengue genes that may be linked to severe disease. Public awareness helped cut household mosquito larvae by 21.65% to 4.45%. Delhi’s sanitation drives and campaigns reduced breeding potential, with Safdarjung Hospital correlating dengue incidence with monsoon-related temperature, rainfall and humidity; September–October are peak months as standing water around homes fosters vector proliferation. An AIIMS-Delhi/PGI-Chandigarh study of 44 children indicated a possible but not conclusive link between COVID infection signs and severe dengue. Prevention remains focused on elimination of standing water and cleanliness.

article.articleHeadline: IIT, ILS secure patent for homegrown TB vaccine
article.articleSummary: TB vaccine KochVac advances in India as IIT Bhubaneswar and ILS Bhubaneswar secure a patent for a protein subunit vaccine against Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The patent 'A Protein Subunit Vaccine Composition Against Mycobacterium tuberculosis' was granted on Nov 16, 2026. The vaccine candidate, developed by Ashis Biswas's team at IIT Bhubaneswar, shows protective efficacy in mouse models, particularly when administered with the existing BCG vaccine. Sunil Raghav’s ILS team evaluated immunogenicity and protection in mice. The candidate has been selected by Tuberculosis Vaccine Initiative and is undergoing further preclinical evaluation in the UK. A four-party technology transfer and commercialization agreement links IIT Bhubaneswar, ILS Bhubaneswar, NRDC, and Techinvention Lifecare Limited of Mumbai. Techinvention Lifecare has begun preclinical animal studies for KochVac, aiming human trials in H2 2027. The program targets enhanced humoral and cell-mediated responses beyond BCG, addressing WHO’s 2024 TB toll of 1.23 million deaths.

article.articleHeadline: Computational Study Identifies Potential Host Furin Cleavage of Toxoplasma
article.articleSummary: Computational study investigates whether Toxoplasma gondii exploits human furin to process invasion-related proteins during entry into intestinal epithelial cells. T. gondii causes toxoplasmosis, infecting roughly one-third of humans globally; congenital toxoplasmosis in India affects about 56,737 infants annually, with 22% of pregnant women infected. The parasite invades via moving junction after secreting microneme and rhoptry proteins, forming a parasitophorous vacuole. The study screens 15 parasite proteins from ToxoDB for furin-like motifs using ProP 1.0 (threshold 0.50), classifying motifs into high (≥0.70), moderate (0.60–0.69), and low (0.50–0.59). Five targets underwent 3D modeling with I-TASSER: TgAMA1, TgRON4, TgMIC8, TgGRA21, TgROP11. Structural validation used Ramachandran plots, ProSA Z-scores, and energy profiling. High-confidence furin motifs were found in ROP11, AMA1, and RON4; MIC8 and GRA21 were moderate. The results suggest host furin could cleave invasion factors, warranting further experimental validation.

triage.headline_ja: 計算科学的研究により、トキソプラズマのタンパク質に対する宿主フーリン切断の可能性が特定される
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は計算機科学的（in silico）基礎研究であり、実際の感染事例やアウトブレイクの報告ではないため、公衆衛生上の緊急性や社会的関心は認められない。
triage.notes: 記事はトキソプラズマ原虫の宿主細胞侵入機構に関する分子生物学的・計算機科学的基礎研究であり、インドにおける先天性トキソプラズマ症の統計は背景情報として言及されているのみで、実際のアウトブレイクや公衆衛生イベントではない。

article.articleHeadline: Dengue fever causes multi-organ failure and vision loss.
article.articleSummary: Two dengue cases in Vietnam illustrate severe organ and ocular complications. At Binh Duong General Hospital, a 1982-born woman (BMI 29) developed dengue shock with recurrent shock, respiratory failure, acute kidney and liver failure after four days of fever. She underwent 45 days of treatment, including 30 days in the ICU, mechanical ventilation, continuous renal replacement therapy, plasma exchange, and multi-organ support. Around two weeks in intensive care, she faced pneumonia from multidrug-resistant bacteria; after about 30 days in ICU, she improved and was moved to internal medicine. In Ho Chi Minh City, an 8-year-old girl developed marked vision loss after dengue, with optic neuritis on MRI. Treated with anti-inflammatory therapy, vision recovered over two weeks (right eye 10/10, left 10/10 by two weeks). Eye complications may occur around day 7 post-onset, even after fever subsides, highlighting dengue’s potential for serious ocular involvement. Published 2026-11-23.

triage.triage_reason: ベトナムで既知の風土病であるデング熱の重症化症例2件の医学的報告であり、新規発生やアウトブレイクを示すものではないため、公衆衛生上のシグナルとしての該当性は低い。
triage.notes: 記事は個別の重症デング熱症例（多臓器不全、視神経炎）に関する医学的報告であり、集団発生や異常な疫学動向を示すものではない。デング熱はベトナムで季節性に流行する既知の疾患であるため、サーベイランス上の新規シグナルとは判断しない。

article.articleHeadline: African swine fever outbreak shows complex developments in Tu My commune
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) outbreak continues in Tu My commune, Ha Tinh Province, Vietnam, with a new cluster detected on 20 November. Since early October, ASF has affected the Son My and Long Thuong hamlets; as of 20 November, authorities have culled 55 pigs (2,828 kg) across Tu My. A new cull of 34 pigs from three households in Son My and Long Thuong occurred on 20 November, with the largest loss being 19 pigs (457 kg) from the household of Lương Thị Thanh Hà in Son My. In Son Ha hamlet, pig deaths of unknown origin have prompted sampling sent to provincial laboratories for confirmation. While awaiting results, local authorities have intensified surveillance, promoted hygiene and farm disinfection, and warned against concealing cases or moving diseased pigs. Sanitation efforts include 3,500 kg of lime and 200 L of chemicals.

article.articleHeadline: Forty airline passengers reported norovirus symptoms.
article.articleSummary: As of 2026-11-23, forty passengers on two airplanes arriving in Europe reported norovirus symptoms. In Germany, authorities declared an emergency at the airport, and medical teams provided care; two passengers required hospitalization as responders acted rapidly. Preliminary data suggest the outbreak may be linked to a cruise ship, with many of the ill travelers having been aboard that vessel. The incident highlights travel-associated transmission of norovirus in international flight hubs. The report also notes that previous coverage denying an 'unknown virus' in Vietnam was corrected; experts emphasize that tourists often fall ill on holidays, including cases of acute respiratory infections (ARVI).

article.articleHeadline: Manila Reports 5,164 Dengue Cases in 2026: Health Department Urges Precautions
article.articleSummary: 5,164 dengue cases in Manila from January–November 2026, per the WILD Diseases Report, with 44 new dengue cases reported on 23 November 2026. The Manila Health Department urges precautions during the rainy season: keep surroundings clean, eliminate stagnant water, stay hydrated, and seek medical attention if symptoms persist. The report also shows 3,284 influenza-like illness cases in Manila (26 new on 23 Nov) and 94 typhoid fever cases (one new), with no new cholera, COVID-19, severe acute respiratory infection, or leptospirosis. Quezon City records the region’s highest dengue burden with 7,652 cases and 43 deaths as of November 2026. The data underscore ongoing dengue transmission in Metro Manila, prompting continued public health guidance to reduce vector habitats and seek care for symptoms.

article.articleHeadline: Mandaue City Council urges weekly clean-ups to prevent dengue fever
article.articleSummary: Mandaue City, Cebu, pushes weekly clean-up drives in schools and barangays to eliminate mosquito breeding sites and curb dengue as cases rise. Councilor Raul Kevin Flores Cabahug announced a resolution and an emergency meeting on Nov 24 at Mandaue City Hall to coordinate dengue responses with the Health Office, Department of Education-Mandaue City Division, and 27 barangays. As of Nov 19, eight dengue-related deaths and about 1,200 dengue cases were recorded, higher than the same period last year. The plan emphasizes rapid post-rain clean-ups and adherence to the DOH '4 o’clock habit,' urging daily searches for and destruction of breeding sites across households. Dengue is a mosquito-borne viral infection causing a severe flu-like illness; warning signs include nausea, vomiting, and rashes. CBC testing is provided free at the City Health Office, underscoring community-wide cooperation for prevention.

article.articleHeadline: Ghanaian Polyherbal Remedies Inhibit Malaria Parasites While Showing
article.articleSummary: Three widely circulated polyherbal antimalarials from urban Ghana inhibit blood-stage Plasmodium falciparum in vitro. Product A (Aloe schweinfurthii, Khaya senegalensis, Piliostigma thonningii, Cassia siamea), Product B (Ocimum viride, Vernonia amygdalina, Morinda lucida, Alstonia boonei, Carica papaya), and Product C (Ananas comosus, Citrus aurantifolia, Azadirachta indica) suppressed chloroquine-sensitive 3D7 trophozoites (IC50: 0.8686, 0.8280, 3.066 µg/mL) and chloroquine-resistant Dd2 trophozoites (0.9388, 0.3177, 15.09 µg/mL). Life-stage tests showed higher schizont IC50s (9.958, 7.707, 13.66) and gametocytes (13.59, 17.92, 59.65), suggesting curative rather than transmission-blocking effects. In non-infected RBCs, CC50s were 117.60, 64.63, 55.23 µg/mL. Ghana FDA requires quality screening and acute toxicity but not efficacy proof; 45 formulations were surveyed in Accra and Kumasi, with three top products selected. Rodent safety was tolerable alongside in vitro efficacy.

article.articleHeadline: Veterinary officers educate students on rabies prevention, responsible pet ownership
article.articleSummary: Rabies prevention education was led in Koforidua, Ghana, on Oct 21, 2026, targeting students at Aboabo Methodist JHS, Wawase R/C JHS, Nkurakan R/C JHS and Nkurakan Presby JHS. Veterinary officers warned that rabies is a viral disease almost always fatal once symptoms appear, mainly transmitted by bites or scratches from dogs and cats. Prevention relies on timely vaccination and prompt medical care after exposure. Animal warning signs include sudden aggression, drooling, restlessness, fear of water, varying difficulty swallowing and unprovoked biting; avoid approaching such animals and report them. Dogs and cats should be regularly vaccinated with records kept; vaccination is not a one-off. From January next year, vaccinated pets in Ghana will receive vaccination cards as part of enforcement. Ghana has started free vaccination for 25,000 dogs and cats in identified high-risk areas to eliminate human deaths from dog-mediated rabies by 2030. Emphasising responsible pet ownership and seeking immediate care after bites.

article.articleHeadline: Onchocerciasis Antibody Levels Decrease With Distance From Blackfly
article.articleSummary: Onchocerciasis transmission around the Simulium damnosum s.l. breeding site near Asubende, Ghana, shows spatial heterogeneity in anti-Ov16 IgG4 seroprevalence. A Sept–Nov 2024 cross-sectional survey across 30 settlements (n=2,479 participants aged ≥3 years) used Ov16 rapid diagnostic tests on dried blood spots to assess exposure. Overall seroprevalence was 10.0% (95% CI 8.9–11.3%), with seropositivity increasing with age and varying by location (0–24.4%). Among 584 children under ten, seroprevalence was 1.5% (95% CI 0.7–2.9%), and after adjusting for test performance, estimated at 0.7% (95% CI 0–2.4%). Seropositive children were detected up to 18 km from the breeding site, but none were found directly at the breeding site. Spatial modeling indicates higher exposure near river habitats. Authors recommend broader spatial sampling beyond riverbank settlements to robustly inform stopping criteria for ivermectin MDA per WHO guidelines.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia : Govt. Encourages Cholera Vaccination Amid Rising Cases
article.articleSummary: Cholera outbreak in Zambia as of 23 November 2026: 3,584 cases and 81 deaths across seven provinces, Lusaka Province accounting for 2,652 cases. Over the past seven days, daily new cases averaged 69; in the last 24 hours, 60 new cases were reported, including 49 in Lusaka, 7 Copperbelt, 2 Southern, and 2 Northern. Since the outbreak was declared on 30 September 2026, 3,004 patients have recovered and been discharged. About 78% of cases were unvaccinated. In response, the government activated the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre and deployed rapid response and emergency medical teams; vaccination campaigns are encouraged in communities with new infections, with support sought from cooperating partners and stakeholders. Ongoing transmission remains very high, underscoring vaccination and public health measures as central to control.

article.articleHeadline: Zambia Records 60 New Cholera Cases, Two Deaths - ZNBC
article.articleSummary: Zambia reports 60 new cholera cases and two deaths in the last 24 hours across four provinces, bringing the total to 3,584, with Lusaka Province accounting for 2,632 cases and forming the outbreak epicentre. Infections continue in Lusaka districts including Mandevu, Kanyama, Munali, Lusaka Central and Chawama. Health authorities warn of deaths in communities due to late treatment. Government actions are led by the National Disaster Management and Mitigation Unit to mobilise resources and coordinate response. The Ministry of Health and ZNPHI will strengthen case management and accelerate vaccination; the Ministry of Water will ensure safe water and sanitation; Education will bolster hygiene screening in schools; Local Government will improve waste collection and close food premises not meeting health standards; efforts include emptying pit latrines and burying shallow wells. At Kafue College of Nursing, 11 cases have been identified, four in the last 24 hours. Public urged to observe hygiene guidelines.
